scope.current_boundary: Teach the principle of conservation of energy in depth, physical mechanisms of energy dissipation into non-useful thermal stores, degraded energy, the formal definition of efficiency as the ratio of useful energy output to total energy input, percentage efficiency, the power formulation of efficiency, quantitative Sankey diagrams, multi-stage systems, and problem-solving with useful and wasted power. Do not pre-teach the formal definition of power as work done per unit time (outcome 9702_t05_m01_o05), algebraic derivation of P = Fv (outcome 9702_t05_m01_o07), or gravitational and kinetic energy derivations (module 9702_t05_cm02).
prior_scope_summaries_consulted: Assumes mastery of work done W = Fs cos theta and mechanical energy transfer from lesson 9702_t05_cm01_l01, weight W = mg from Topic 3, and kinematics from Topic 2.

immediate_previous.boundary: Understand the concept of work, W = Fs cos theta, and work done by expanding gas W = p Delta V.
can_assume: definition of work done as force multiplied by displacement in direction of force
W = Fs cos theta and conditions for positive, negative, zero work
W = p Delta V for gas expansion
work done equals mechanical energy transferred

immediate_next.boundary: Definition of power as work done per unit time and problem solving with P = W / t.
must_not_preteach: formal definition of power as work done or energy transferred per unit time (9702_def_power)
derivation and extensive problem solving with P = Fv
